_meta.indication: Treatment of generalized pustular psoriasis (GPP) flares in adults

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to a single 900 mg intravenous dose of spesolimab or placebo on Day 1
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with GPP flare of moderate-to-severe intensity (GPPPGA total score of at least 3), presence of fresh pustules, GPPPGA pustulation subscore of at least 2, and at least 5% body surface area covered with erythema and pustules
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with a GPPPGA pustulation subscore of 0 (indicating no visible pustules) at Week 1 after treatment
pivotal_trials.n: 53 subjects randomized: spesolimab N=35, placebo N=18
pivotal_trials.result: Spesolimab superior to placebo on GPPPGA pustulation subscore of 0 at Week 1 (54% vs 6%; one-sided p-value = 0.0004)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) are asthenia and fatigue (9%), nausea and vomiting (9%), headache (9%), pruritus and prurigo (6%), infusion site hematoma and bruising (6%), and urinary tract infection (6%). Infections occurred in 14% of SPEVIGO subjects vs 6% placebo through Week 1. Serious hypersensitivity reactions including DRESS were reported in two subjects exposed to spesolimab in trial 1368-0013.
target_moa: Humanized monoclonal IgG1 antibody that inhibits interleukin-36 (IL-36) signaling by specifically binding to the IL-36 receptor (IL36R), preventing activation of IL36R by cognate ligands (IL-36 alpha, beta and gamma) and downstream activation of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic pathways

rems.type: A Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is not needed

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not presented to an Advisory Committee or other external consult
